chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Wasiti from Qasim al-Sayqal who said:

I wrote to Al-Reza (peace be upon him), 'I manufacture the sheaths for the swords from the skins of dead donkeys, and my clothes get hit. So can I pray in these?' So he (peace be upon him) wrote to me: 'Take (other) clothes for your prayer'.

So I wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) the 2nd, 'I had written to your father (peace be upon him) with such and such. So that was difficult upon me, so I started making these from the skins of wild donkeys properly slaughtered'. So he (peace be upon him) wrote to me: 'Every righteous work is with patience. May Allah have Mercy on you. So it was such that what you are making is of wild (donkeys), slaughtered, so there is no problem'.
ai.seo_question: Is clothing made from the skins of slaughtered wild animals considered pure for prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith illustrates the jurisprudential nuance between the two Imams regarding the purity of leather from wild animals (dhakīyah) versus domestic donkeys (khayl al-maytah). Imam al-Ridha initially advised changing garments to avoid doubt, while Imam al-Jawad clarified that wild animals slaughtered properly yield pure leather, highlighting the Shia principle of distinguishing between different categories of animal skins in ritual purity.

en.sarwar: 16. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah al-Wasitiy, from al-Qasim al-Sayqal who has said the following:

“I once wrote to al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘I make sword sheathing of leather from dead donkeys. My clothes come in contact with it and I perform Salah (prayer) with them. He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, wrote to me, ‘Find other clothes for your Salah (prayer).’

I then wrote to abu Ja’far, the second, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘I would write to your father, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about such and such issues. It became difficult for me and I then began to make them from leather of wild donkeys, properly slaughtered.’ He (the Imam) wrote to me, ‘All good deeds require patience, I pray to Allah to grant you blessings. If what you do is from wild ones and properly slaughtered, then it is not harmful.’”
